chunks: It is narrated from Al-Arqaṭ, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said:

Do not be one who constantly roams in the markets, and do not personally take charge of buying trivial items yourself. For it does not befit the Muslim man possessing religion and lineage to personally handle the purchase of minor goods, except for three things. For it befits one possessing religion and lineage to handle them himself: real estate, camels, and slaves.

key_terms.الْأَسْوَاقِ: the markets, as places of buying and selling
key_terms.الْحَسَبِ: social standing, honor, or noble repute
key_terms.ذِي الدِّينِ: one possessing religion and upright faith

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teach about personal involvement in buying goods in the market?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches dignified conduct in livelihood and market dealings. It discourages a man of religion and standing from busying himself with the direct purchase of trivial goods, while recommending that he personally oversee major and consequential purchases.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3639 - It is narrated from Al-Arqat that Abu Abdillah (as) said:

"Do not spend your time wandering through markets, nor personally handle the purchase of minor goods. It does not befit a Muslim who possesses faith and honor to involve himself directly in purchasing small items-except in three matters.
It is proper for a man of faith and dignity to personally handle these three matters: buying real estate, camels, and slaves."
